description: W_lambda transfer-matrix reformulation of binding: validates the defect-cubic gate (n=7 Z-crossing), the deuteron single-bond bracket (#2528), and the connected-part mechanism (diagonal/disjoint=0, braided!=0). Fit-free; NOT a binding closure.

assertions.name: defect_cubic_sign_flip_at_n7
assertions.detail: 1-Z>0 for n=2..6 (True); 1-Z<0 appears by n=7..9 (True) -> matches Lean 144C(n)=-n(n-1)(2n-13)

assertions.name: deuteron_fpn_bracketed_by_single_bond_Wlambda
assertions.detail: bare 0.395 < f_pn 0.588 < W_(2,1)=0.660674 (single bond UNDER-binds; gap 0.193 = connected term)

assertions.name: disjoint_bonds_connected_zero
assertions.detail: tr(2 disjoint bonds) - tr(b)^2 = 0.0 (diagonal/commuting W_lambda transfer matrix cannot be extensive)

assertions.name: braided_crossings_connected_nonzero
assertions.detail: tr(sigma^2) - tr(sigma)^2 = 0.752702 != 0 (the topological/extensive channel lives in the NON-commuting braid)

result.verdict: MECHANISM PINNED (no closure): the W_lambda transfer matrix's trace carries the Lean-proved defect-cubic (n=7 Z-crossing); the deuteron single-bond W_(2,1) brackets f_pn from above (gap = connected term); and the connected part is ZERO for diagonal/disjoint bonds but NONZERO for braided/repeated crossings -> extensivity must come from the non-commuting braid transfer matrix with W_lambda injected per block, NOT from the scalar weighted trace. Not a binding closure.
